parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Unique key you generate for this attempt (e.g. a UUID). Optional: without it every call is a new request. Resending the same key (after a timeout or network cut) returns the original response instead of creating a second operation; the same key with a different body, or while the first call is still in progress, returns 409.

example_prompt: Let the customer retry a failed SasPay payment, optionally on another network.

methods.description: Codes réseau à essayer, dans l'ordre. Défaut : réseau d'origine de la transaction.

gotchas: SasPay has no working sandbox. Its docs say an sk_test_ key is SANDBOX, "tests sans argent réel" (docs.saspay.me/account-setup), but after a card payment made with such a key was debited for real (maintainer's test, 2026-11-01), SasPay's support answered « les clés sandbox ne sont pas fonctionnelles, veuillez utiliser les clés lives » (reply to the maintainer's ticket of 2026-11-01, read 2026-11-07). Treat every call as production: test with amounts you accept to pay or send, and never tell a tester that an sk_test_ key means no money moves. The verification recorded on this spec (environment: sandbox) was run with an sk_test_ key on 2026-10-17: that label is what test:live records for such a key, not proof of a separate test environment; the API answered normally, and whether such a key moves money on mobile money is not known.
Retrying reuses the same transaction and id; it never creates a new transaction.
Only incoming payments can be retried: a payout returns 400. A FAILED payment is retryable (that is what this endpoint is for); 409 is for the other terminal states.
Send an Idempotency-Key: without it a network retry relaunches the payment a second time. Reusing a key with a different body, or while the first call is still running, returns 409.

The retry can switch the customer to a hosted page: with an sk_test_ key (live test 2026-10-17), a failed mtn_ci push retried with no body came back with a checkout_url (status still FAILED until the customer pays), so check checkout_url on every retry.

spans: ne crée jamais de nouvelle transaction, réutilise le même `id`.
La transaction ciblée est un flux sortant (payout), non réessayable via cet endpoint
sans lui, un retry réseau relance une seconde fois le paiement.
Même clé, 1<sup>er</sup> appel encore en cours
